Gantry Stand: Assembly

Bench box + wheeled cart, 80/20 10-series. Generated from gantry_cart.py; all lengths in inches.

The finished stand

Parts added in a step New 4132 bracketsAlready built

Before you start: the 3393 bolt kits use slide-in economy T-nuts. They can only enter a slot from an open end, and many ends get closed off as the frame goes together. For each member, slide in every T-nut it will need (table below) before you join it, threading the bolt through the bracket a turn or two so the nut stays put. 127 T-nuts in all: 96 from the 3393 kits, 22 3382s for the locators, 8 from the 3321 kits and 1 for the ball head.

Orientation used throughout: front and back are the two long sides of the cart; the laptop side is the end with the laptop table (the gantry's leg-rail motor end); the mast side is the opposite end, where the camera mast goes.

1Shelf ring and postsBench box

  1. Work on a flat bench, right way up: the box bottom is the posts' bottoms and the shelf rails' bottoms, all flush.
  2. Fit the four C 20 in rails between the four D posts, flush with the post bottoms and with the outside faces.
  3. Join each rail end to its post with a 4132 on the inside face of the rail (8 brackets). Nothing sticks out below the box.
  4. Before the front and back rails are closed in, slide 2 extra T-nuts into each one's top slot for the shelf-panel screws (step 2), roughly 3 in and 21 in from the laptop-side end.

2Shelf panelBench box

  1. Notch the 24 x 24 in black ACM panel 2 x 2 in at all four corners so it fits around the posts.
  2. Drill four 17/64 in clearance holes (no countersink: the 3321 is a flanged button head that sits on the panel) 0.5 in in from the front and back edges, at 3 in and 21 in from the laptop-side edge. (Mark them off the T-nuts if they've drifted.)
  3. Lay it on the shelf rails and fix with four 3321 flat-head screws into the T-nuts pre-loaded in the front and back rails.
  4. Do this now: once the top frame is on, the panel can't get past it.

3Top frameBench box

  1. Lay out the two A 24 in rails (front and back) and fit the two B 22 in rails between their ends.
  2. Join each corner with a 4132 on the inside face of the B rail (4 brackets), flush top and bottom.
  3. Load the T-nuts for step 4 now (table): every rail needs 2 in its bottom slot, one per post bracket.
  4. Square it: the diagonals should match. This frame is the breadboard's footprint, flush with its edges.

4Top frame onto the postsBench box

  1. Set the top frame on the four posts, outside faces flush all round.
  2. Fix each post with two 4132s (8 in all): one flange under the rail above it, the other on the post's inside face.
  3. The post T-nuts for these brackets can still go in from the post bottoms (a different slot from the shelf brackets' nuts), but it's easier to load them first.

5Camera mast and boomBench box

  1. Stand the E mast against the mast side (the end without the laptop table) at mid-depth, bottom flush with the box bottom.
  2. Bolt it to the top-frame and shelf side rails with four 4132s, one each side of the mast at each rail.
  3. Fit the F boom to the mast's inside face with one 4132 under it and one on top; loosen both to slide the boom up or down.
  4. Keep the boom's top at least 1 in below the mast top, or the upper bracket has nothing to bolt to. (The CAD had them flush; 1 in down puts the lens 35 in above the board.)
  5. Put one T-nut in the boom's bottom slot ~1 in from its free end (over the board centre) for the ball-head stud, then fit the camera.

6Legs and lower ringWheeled cart

  1. Stand the four K legs upright and fit the four J 20 in rails between them, outside faces flush.
  2. Rail bottoms 3.0 in above the leg bottoms: cut two 3.0 in spacer blocks and stand the rails on them while you tighten.
  3. Join with 4132s on the rails' inside faces (8 brackets), same as the box shelf ring.
  4. Tap two corner holes 1/4-20 in each leg's bottom end now (step 8 shows which), while the legs are easy to handle.

7Cart top frameWheeled cart

  1. Lay the two G 38 in rails front and back, and fit three H 22 in rails between them: one over each end of the leg square and one at the far end of the 14 in run-on (the laptop end).
  2. Join with 4132s on the inside faces of the H rails (6 brackets).
  3. Pre-load the T-nuts in the table, including 2 in each G rail's top slot under the laptop table (1.5 in and 12.5 in from the leg square) and the locator nuts in the outside slots of the rails and legs (step 9).
  4. Set the frame on the legs, run-on toward the laptop side, and fix each leg with two 4132s under the rails (8 brackets).

8CastersWheeled cart

  1. Turn the cart over (top frame down, on cardboard).
  2. Each 2419 plate sits 0.5 in inboard of the leg centre, toward the middle of the cart front-to-back, so two of its counterbored holes land on two of the leg's corner holes. Tap those two holes 1/4-20 and fix with 1/4-20 x 3/4 SHCS, heads in the counterbores.
  3. Bolt each 2323 caster to its plate with four 5/16-18 x 5/8 SHCS, long side of the flange along the cart's length.
  4. Only two screws hold each plate to its leg: snug them firmly and re-check after the first few moves.

From below: the plate is shifted 0.5 in toward the middle of the cart front-to-back, so two of its holes meet two corner holes in the leg end.

9Locators, laptop table, end capsWheeled cart

  1. Stand the cart on its wheels and lock the brakes.
  2. Bolt a 4166 flat plate (3 x 2 in, 6 holes) upright on the outside of each leg top, flush with the corner and standing 1.0 in above the cart top, with a 1/32 in shim behind it (box clearance). The top row of holes stays empty; the middle row goes into the top rail's slot and the bottom row into the leg's two slots. Mast-side corners get a plate on both faces: front/back 4 bolts, end 3 (its middle-row corner hole is over the rail end, no slot). Laptop-side corners: front/back plate only, 4 bolts.
  3. Drill 17/64 in clearance holes (no countersink) in the 13.84 x 24 in laptop panel for four 3321 screws (0.5 in from the long edges, at 1.5 in and 12.5 in from its box end) and fix it to the G rails.
  4. Push 2015 end caps onto the two open G rail ends at the laptop end.

10Lift the box onto the cartFinal

  1. Lock the casters. With two people, lower the bench box straight down into the four corner locators.
  2. Mount the breadboard + gantry on the top frame: the gantry legs' M4 nuts (under the board's outermost hole rows, 8.5, 15.5 and 22.5 in from the motor-end edge) slide into the top slots of the A rails from their ends. The legs' far ends overhang the board's mast-side edge by about 5/8 in.
  3. Then push 2015 end caps onto the four A rail ends.
  4. The board top ends up 30 in above the floor; the laptop table is at 24.03 in.
